fr:title.text: Recap: amazing right adjoint to a single character

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Recap: amazing right adjoint to a single character

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Recall from Grammar/Derivative/Base.agda that for a character c the right Brzozowski derivative is the linear residual D_l\, A\, c \;=\; A \mathbin {\htmlStyle {display:inline-block;transform:rotate(180deg);}{\multimap }} \texttt {"}c\texttt {"}. The "amazing right adjoint" — the further right adjoint, in the sense of the tiny-object story — is given by
with the symmetric variant
when the character sits at the end of a string. These already exist in the codebase as √l c A and √r c A, with √l-app witnessing the counit D_l\, (\sqrt {c}\, A)\, c \vdash A.

The amazing-right-adjoint construction goes through for any tiny object, not only single characters. In the grammar setting strings are tiny: an inhabited string is a finite product of literal grammars under \otimes , and \texttt {"}c\texttt {"} \otimes - preserves all colimits, so iterating gives a left adjoint \texttt {String}\, w \otimes - with both adjoints on the right.

Notation. For a non-empty string w, write \sqrt [w]{A} for the right-adjoint indexed over w; concretely \sqrt [w]{A} \;=\; (\texttt {String}\, w \otimes \top ) \Rightarrow (\texttt {String}\, w \otimes A) on the left-handed side, with the obvious right-handed dual. The single-character √l c A is the special case w = [c].

Define \rhd A \;:=\; \mathchoice {\textstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}\sqrt [w]{A}. A point of ▷ A is a coherent family: for every non-empty string w, a witness that consuming a w-prefix exposes an A. The indexing is by all non-empty strings simultaneously, so the modality is character-agnostic in the same sense as classical guarded type theory's ▷, while being grounded in concrete suffix-extraction at every non-empty depth.
Two design questions are baked into the definition.

html:ul.html:li: Side. We pick the left-handed \sqrt [w]{}, which encodes "any proper suffix"; the right-handed choice gives "any proper prefix". They are symmetric and either could serve. A genuinely two-sided ▷ encoding "any proper substring" is the natural next target — see TODOs below.

Why non-empty. Empty w would give \sqrt [\epsilon ]{A} \cong A, collapsing \rhd A \vdash A into a strict identity and killing Löb. Restricting to non-empty strings keeps the modality genuinely "later".

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The candidate is only useful if it has the structural rules of a later modality. Three properties to check.

html:ol.html:li: Next. A canonical map \mathsf {next} : A \vdash \rhd A. Heuristic construction: for each non-empty w the component should factor through the strength of \sqrt [w]{} on A, packaging the universal property of the amazing right adjoint with the splitting \texttt {String}\, w \otimes \top \vdash \texttt {String}\, w \otimes A that already holds when A is global.

Functoriality and \sqrt {}-applicativity. Since ▷ is a \And -indexed limit of right adjoints it is automatically a right adjoint, hence preserves limits. The genuinely calculus-specific check is the interaction with \otimes : do we get \rhd (A \otimes B) \vdash \rhd A \otimes \rhd B, or its dual, in a way that lets later-style applicative bookkeeping go through?

Löb induction. (\rhd A \vdash A) \;\Rightarrow \; (\top \vdash A). Conjectural argument sketch: from \rhd A \vdash A and next build \rhd A \vdash \rhd A as a \sqrt [w]{}-coalgebra in each component; uniqueness on each component forces the global fixed point, and the limit of "the unique fixed point" is the unique fixed point of the limit. The character-by-character flavor of this matches the well-founded-on-string-length argument used in sss-00A8 to build the Brzozowski parser, suggesting that Löb here is in fact the same principle, repackaged.

fr:title.text: Resolution: next is structure, not a theorem

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Resolution: next is structure, not a theorem

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The diagram chase does not go through for arbitrary grammars — the verification check anticipated above fails. next is not derivable from the indexed-product definition of ▷ alone; it requires extra structure on A.

Max's framing. Presheaves on (\texttt {String}, \text {suffix-order}) are precisely \Box -coalgebras over families. The map next : A ⊢ ▷ A is the coalgebra structure, not a global term. So instead of postulating it (or holding it open as a hole), package it as a record:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: record IsCoalgebra (A : Grammar ℓA) : Type ℓA where field next : A ⊢ ▷ A
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The canonical example is ⊤-IsCoalgebra: ⊤ is suffix-closed because any suffix of a ⊤-parse is a ⊤-parse. This lives in Grammar/Later/Coalgebra.agda on the guarded branch of gsa-brzozowski.

html:ul.html:li: Grammar/Later/Base.agda now compiles without --allow-unsolved-metas — the held-open next hole is gone.
Löb (sss-00BE) goes through unchanged: the obstruction to next does not block Löb, because Löb is proven directly by well-founded recursion on string length and never invokes a global next.

This is the same shape of design discovery as Cass's recursive-coalgebra framework: well-foundedness + recursion lives on coalgebra structures, not on bare grammars. The connection is made explicit in the recursive-coalgebra synthesis — next is the coalgebra structure that feeds a c2a-morphism.

fr:title.text: State and Attempt Löb Induction for ▷

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: State and Attempt Löb Induction for ▷

fr:mainmatter.html:p: State and attempt the Löb induction principle lob : (▷ A ⊢ A) → (⊤ ⊢ A) for the candidate ▷ of sss-00B9. This is the test of the whole approach: if Löb holds, the modality is genuinely "later"; if it fails, examine why before fixing the definition.

Sketch to follow. From ▷ A ⊢ A and next (sss-00BD) build \rhd A \vdash \rhd A as a \sqrt [w]{}-coalgebra in each component; uniqueness on each component forces the global fixed point, and the limit of "the unique fixed point" is the unique fixed point of the limit.

Compare against sss-00A8. The character-by- character flavour of the proof matches the well-founded-on-string-length recursion already used to build the Brzozowski parser. If the proof goes through, check whether it reuses that recursion verbatim — that would be evidence Löb here is the same principle, repackaged as a type former.

The empty-string boundary may sneak back in via the limit, even though we excluded it from the indexing.
Composing two limits (the indexed product and the recursive fixed point) may need a Fubini-style commutation that is genuinely nontrivial.

fr:title.text: Resolution: next is structure, not a theorem

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Resolution: next is structure, not a theorem

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The diagram chase does not go through for arbitrary grammars — the verification check anticipated above fails. next is not derivable from the indexed-product definition of ▷ alone; it requires extra structure on A.

Max's framing. Presheaves on (\texttt {String}, \text {suffix-order}) are precisely \Box -coalgebras over families. The map next : A ⊢ ▷ A is the coalgebra structure, not a global term. So instead of postulating it (or holding it open as a hole), package it as a record:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: record IsCoalgebra (A : Grammar ℓA) : Type ℓA where field next : A ⊢ ▷ A
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The canonical example is ⊤-IsCoalgebra: ⊤ is suffix-closed because any suffix of a ⊤-parse is a ⊤-parse. This lives in Grammar/Later/Coalgebra.agda on the guarded branch of gsa-brzozowski.

html:ul.html:li: Grammar/Later/Base.agda now compiles without --allow-unsolved-metas — the held-open next hole is gone.
Löb (sss-00BE) goes through unchanged: the obstruction to next does not block Löb, because Löb is proven directly by well-founded recursion on string length and never invokes a global next.

This is the same shape of design discovery as Cass's recursive-coalgebra framework: well-foundedness + recursion lives on coalgebra structures, not on bare grammars. The connection is made explicit in the recursive-coalgebra synthesis — next is the coalgebra structure that feeds a c2a-morphism.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Commits: e5038b9 (document obstruction), 38db93f (refactor to IsCoalgebra record).
